entities.summary:
Hervé de Portzmoguer, also known as Primauguet, was a Breton naval officer born around 1472-1482, known for his bravery during the Hundred Years' War. He served as a captain in the French and Breton navies, participating in several battles, including the Battle of Saint-Mathieu in 1512.


De Portzmoguer's significance lies in his role as a prominent naval commander during a pivotal moment in European history. His actions, though often overshadowed by more famous figures, contributed to the shifting balance of power in Western Europe.


The legacy of Hervé de Portzmoguer can be seen in the continued importance of naval warfare and the significance of the Battle of Saint-Mathieu as a turning point in the Hundred Years' War.


Despite his relatively minor status, de Portzmoguer's story serves as a reminder of the countless individuals who played crucial roles in shaping the course of history.

entities.summary:
Hervé de Portzmoguer, also known as 'Primauguet', was a Breton naval officer who played a pivotal role in the medieval maritime landscape of Europe. He was born in 1470 in Plouarzel, Brittany, France, and died in 1512 during the Battle of Saint-Mathieu, where his ship exploded.

  De Portzmoguer's significance lies in his contributions to the development of Breton and French naval capabilities, particularly during the reign of King Louis XI. His bravery and tactical prowess during the Battle of Saint-Mathieu earned him a place in the annals of Breton history.

  The legacy of Hervé de Portzmoguer can be seen in the continued importance of the Breton naval tradition, which has shaped the maritime identity of France and the region. His story serves as a testament to the enduring impact of individual heroism and strategic leadership on the course of history.
